A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PH-Reg research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison, including matching relocated supplementary material.

before.justification: V1 reports original segmentation and depth experiments in Tables 1–2, architectural ablations in Figure 5, and additional Pearson-correlation evaluations in Table S.4.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds component and shift-ratio experiments in Tables 3–4 and efficiency measurements in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The teacher, augmentation-averaged targets, student registers, selective unfreezing and cosine-plus-MSE objective remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 documents the existing denoising procedure. The 15% shift range discussed in v2 was already specified in v1 Appendix B.3.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eight open-vocabulary segmentation benchmarks, VOC21/ADE linear-probe segmentation, NYUv2 depth evaluation and COCO Caption ablations. The added studies vary components and internal denoising augmentations within retained coverage.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1, 2 and S.4 are retained. New comparisons include standalone MaskCLIP with 10-fold averaging in Table 3 and NACLIP with 10-fold denoising in Table S.7.

E3.justification: V2 adds component-removal controls, a 0–30% shift sweep, a matched single-GPU DINOv2 ViT-B timing protocol, and fp32/eager-attention inference-cost evaluation. Existing benchmark preprocessing, linear-probe settings and default training configurations remain unchanged; the single-GPU restriction belongs to the new timing study.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands validation of the design: Table 3 isolates distillation, denoising and registers using downstream segmentation scores; Table 4 tests shift sensitivity; Appendix D analyzes training time, storage and inference cost. These supplement the retained register-count, layer-unfreezing, augmentation-count and artifact-norm analyses.

E5.justification: The existing feature-percentile reporting in Figure 5 is retained. V2 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises eight DVT segmentation entries: for example, OpenCLIP+DVT VOC21 mIoU changes from 71.03 to 72.58, and DFN-CLIP+DVT from 70.47 to 73.09, now exceeding PH-Reg's unchanged 72.97. The accompanying comparison narrows from five of six backbones to at least four. Tables 3–4 and S.6–S.7 add substantive component, sensitivity and efficiency results, including 150 versus 365.1 hours for PH-Reg and DVT.

T1.justification: The optimal-feature-aggregation proof moves from Appendix F to G but retains the same squared-error objective, derivation and arithmetic-mean minimizer. Patch-level wording and equivalent notation changes do not introduce a new mathematical result or assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: efficient post-training integration of registers, artifact reduction without labeled data or full retraining, and improved dense prediction. The added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds an interpretation attributing roughly half the improvement each to registers and denoising, although Table 3 does not clearly support that attribution. It also justifies the retained 15% shift choice and extends the discussion of models benefiting from DVT's residual estimator to DFN-CLIP. The limitations paragraph is unchanged.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 makes the existing accumulation/counting procedure explicit. Appendix D documents efficiency-measurement settings, runtime, storage and implementation choices. Appendix B now states that model weights, as well as code, are available; existing training hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations concerning attention sinks, untrained registers, dense-feature brain mapping and COCO Captions. The original references and broad positioning against register training, neural-field denoising and attention modifications remain.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized abstract, author-header, terminology and heading edits, adds procedural explanation, and separates the retained artifact discussion into Section 4.4. Appendix organization changes to accommodate efficiency analysis, but most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands and rearranges the displays through Algorithm 1, Tables 3–4 and Tables S.6–S.7. Figures 6–7 move, Figure 2's coordinate labels change, and several existing supplementary figures are grouped onto shared pages. The qualitative examples are retained rather than removed.

improvement.justification: V2 improves assessability through downstream component tests, shift sensitivity, explicit efficiency measurements and denoising pseudocode. The revised comparison also acknowledges a DFN-CLIP result favoring DVT. These benefits are tempered by the new equal-contribution explanation: Table 3 shows only 0.37 average mIoU points from adding registers to denoised distillation, versus 1.19 from adding denoising with registers. The added evidence provides a limited net improvement despite this interpretive weakness.
